headline: Bills 26, Dolphins 9

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Buffalo built a 20–3 lead before Miami’s defense forced back-to-back interceptions late in the first half — but the offense turned those takeaways into just three points. Miami closed to 20–9 after halftime, then Buffalo stuffed Kyle McCord on fourth-and-2 to end the comeback.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Rookie Jacob Rodriguez had 13 tackles and an interception. Zayne Anderson added 11 tackles, a pick and a sack. Ollie Gordon II averaged 6.3 yards a carry for 69 yards.

body.label: Injury/roster news
body.text: Chris Bell briefly left with a chest injury but returned. Punter Bradley Pinion and receiver Jared Wayne were out, and Malik Willis remains on injured reserve with a groin/core injury.

body.label: Big Sarge's take
body.text: Two picks off Josh Allen, three sacks, and the defense gave you every chance — and the offense answered with 185 yards and zero touchdowns. You can’t keep asking that defense to win games the offense refuses to show up for. The gap between the two units is the whole story of this season now.

next: New York Jets at Miami — Sunday, Nov 29, 1:00 PM ET on CBS

hurricanes.headline: No. 7 Miami 28, Virginia Tech 20

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Miami fell behind 14–0 after an early Darian Mensah interception. Jake Weinberg’s school-record 59-yard field goal cut the halftime deficit to three, then Mark Fletcher Jr. capped a 17-play, 90-yard drive for Miami’s first lead and added an 11-yard insurance touchdown.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Fletcher ran for three touchdowns. Mensah shook off two interceptions to throw for 241 yards, and Cooper Barkate caught seven for 72. Weinberg’s 59-yarder broke Miami’s previous record of 57.

body.label: Injury news
body.text: Fletcher showed no lingering effects from the lower-body issue that limited him against Duke. Malachi Toney remained out after ankle surgery; no significant new injury was reported.

body.label: Big Sarge's take
body.text: Ten and one, 8–0 in the league, and a spot in the ACC Championship Game — first one since 2017. That’s a program back where it belongs. But spot elite teams 14–0 in the playoff and you won’t climb out. Start faster, protect the ball, and this team can play with anybody. Keep digging holes and January gets short.

hurricanes.next: Boston College at Miami — Saturday, Nov 28, noon ET on ESPN; then Wake Forest for the ACC Championship on Dec 5.
